- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is falling, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid under-shoot.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong price declines — if true outcome shows mean reversion, forecast should be slightly below model’s peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in early periods when sentiment is volatile — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.1) and model forecasts remain flat, consider slight upward bias to avoid prolonged underestimation.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to anticipate reversal — adjust forecast downward 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
